transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8, and before I sign off on the approval, I want to make sure we've thoroughly reviewed the plan from all angles. The draft currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you on any concerns or recommendations related to your area of expertise. Let's start with you — what should I be thinking about as we look at this proposal?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Singh. I appreciate the opportunity to weigh in. I do have an important staffing concern I'd like to raise. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it shows we have 18 student tutors signed up for this program. The school's supervision rule states that one adult can supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. With 18 tutors, two adult supervisors would only cover 12 students — that leaves us six tutors short of adequate supervision. I think we need to either add a third supervisor or revisit how we structure the sessions to stay compliant with the supervision ratio. I'd recommend we update the draft plan to reflect the actual roster numbers and adjust staffing accordingly before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings in the draft plan. This week, I completed a student-support review as part of my counseling responsibilities, and I found two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students who are seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so this information wouldn't be visible to anyone else reviewing the roster. Because of these restrictions, we cannot allow students to self-select their tutor pairings — if they did, there's a real risk that a restricted pairing could be created, violating those no-contact orders. I need to recommend that the plan be revised so that all tutor pairings are assigned and actively monitored by me as the counselor, rather than being student-selected. This is both a student safety issue and a compliance issue that we need to address before Dr. Singh signs off on approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical technology concern about the draft plan's use of Google Classroom for session communication. Google Classroom is not approved for this program's student-to-student communication. The district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment is the approved platform, and it retains the required school records. I confirmed the platform settings with district IT this week, but the technology field in the draft application has not yet been updated to reflect this. Before Dr. Singh signs off on approval, the draft plan needs to be revised to specify Microsoft Teams instead of Google Classroom for all session communication.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern about the consent form process described in the draft plan. I confirmed the procedure with the family-engagement office this week, and for this program, family consent must be entered in the student information system before a student participates. The district has also approved translated electronic forms in addition to paper forms, so families who need translated materials can use those. However, the draft plan still describes only paper consent form collection without any SIS entry. This needs to be revised before approval so that the plan reflects both the SIS entry requirement and the availability of translated electronic forms.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.consent_record: SIS entry required; translated electronic forms available in addition to paper forms

commitments.detail: Update the draft plan to reflect 18 tutors on the roster and assign three adult supervisors to meet the 1:6 supervision ratio.
Revise the plan so all tutor pairings are assigned and actively monitored by the counselor, replacing student-selected pairings.
Update the technology field in the draft application to specify Microsoft Teams instead of Google Classroom for all session communication.
Revise the consent process to require SIS entry before participation and include availability of translated electronic forms alongside paper forms.
